title: U.S. Measles Cases Hit a 35-Year High
hook: The CDC has confirmed 2,318 measles cases this year — the most since 1991, and the second record-breaking year in a row for a disease the U.S. once declared eliminated.
key_points: The CDC confirmed 2,318 U.S. measles cases, the highest annual count since 1991.
It's the second consecutive year the U.S. has set a modern record for measles.
Measles was declared eliminated in the U.S. in 2000 — sustained spread means that status is under strain.
Measles is one of the most contagious diseases known and spreads through the air before a rash appears.
Two doses of the MMR vaccine are about 97% effective at preventing measles.
Falling childhood vaccination coverage is what lets clusters turn into outbreaks.
content_html: For the second year in a row, the U.S. has set a modern record for measles. The CDC announced that the country has now confirmed 2,318 cases this year — the highest count since 1991, three and a half decades ago.
extra_html:
That number lands strangely against history: the U.S. declared measles eliminated in 2000, meaning the virus was no longer continuously circulating here. Getting back to a 35-year high takes a specific kind of failure. Measles is one of the most contagious diseases known to medicine, and it spreads through the air — including in the days before the characteristic rash shows up, when nobody knows to stay home. Against a pathogen that transmissible, herd immunity has almost no slack in it: two doses of MMR are roughly 97% effective, so outbreaks of this size reflect falling vaccination coverage rather than a vaccine that stopped working.

The practical version, per public health officials: check that you and your kids are up to date on MMR, especially before travel, and treat a measles exposure as something to call a clinician about rather than wait out.

related.title: Vaccines Adults Still Need
related.hook: Vaccination isn't just a childhood checklist. Protection from some shots fades, new ones are recommended with age, and a few need regular boosters.

related.title: An Experimental Pill That Stopped a Measles-Like Virus From Spreading
related.hook: A drug called GHP-88310 blocked airborne spread of a measles-like virus in ferrets — the first time a polymerase inhibitor has done that. It could one day shut outbreaks down, not replace vaccines.

related.title: Flu and Seasonal Shots
related.hook: Some vaccines are a yearly habit, not a one-time event — because the viruses change, or immunity fades, and a fresh shot keeps protection current each season.

flashcards.prompt: Why does measles come back so quickly when vaccination coverage slips?
flashcards.back_html: It's among the most contagious diseases known and spreads through the air — including before the telltale rash appears. That combination means even small gaps in coverage let a single case seed an outbreak.

flashcards.prompt: How well does the MMR vaccine protect against measles?
flashcards.back_html: Two doses are about 97% effective at preventing measles — which is why sustained outbreaks are a coverage problem, not a vaccine-failure problem.
